## Protocol and honest notes

- **Models**: Mistral-7B-v0.1 (MHA-ish GQA 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, 32 layers) and Qwen3-8B (GQA 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, 36 layers). fp16 weights, HF transformers 4.51.3, sdpa attention. Quantisation is fake-quant (quantise on cache write, dequantised values read back), so numbers are *accuracy* only; bytes/vec is the analytic packed size incl. scales.
- **ppl**: WikiText-2 test, 8 non-overlapping 2048-token windows; first 1024 tokens via chunked prefill (chunk 256), remaining 1023 via token-by-token teacher-forced decode, all through the quantised cache; `dppl` = delta vs fp16 on WikiText-2. C4: first 400 docs of validation shard 0, 4 windows (same protocol). Small sample: differences < ~0.02 ppl are noise.
- **attn**: last 128 queries of a 2048-token WikiText prefix, real post-RoPE K/V and real queries, attention output of fp16 K/V vs fake-quantised K/V, mean over layers (cos / rel. L2 error).
- **needle**: passkey (5 digits) in repetitive filler, depths 0.1/0.5/0.9 x 2 seeds = 6 prompts per length, prefill chunked 2048, greedy decode through quantised cache. Mistral-7B-v0.1 is NOT trained for >8k (fp16 itself fails at 16k/32k), so only Qwen3-8B is informative at 16k/32k; Mistral numbers are relative to its own fp16. Only 6 prompts per cell: resolution 0.17.
- **multikey / kv-ret**: our own RULER-style synthetic tasks (multi-key NIAH with 4 magic numbers; UUID key-value retrieval, Liu et al.), 6 prompts/cell, lengths 4k/8k/16k. NOT official RULER/LongBench numbers (no dataset download; synthetic generators in qeval.py).
- **verify (K=1..8)**: 200 disjoint 512-token WikiText-2 prompts. fp16 greedy continuation g1..g8; quantised-cache model prefills prompt[:-1] then verifies the block [p_last, g1..g7] in ONE multi-query forward; `match@K` = mean token agreement with fp16 over the first K positions, `accept@K` = P(first K all agree). Because attention is causal, the K<8 numbers are prefixes of the same pass. The fp16 row (~0.998) is the numerical noise floor (batched/chunked vs sequential kernels flip near-tie argmaxes).
- **kinds**: `official` = repo `uqmt.attn.quantize_fp4`; `official-port` = amd-experiments kernels (TurboQuant WHT-free random-orthogonal rotation + Lloyd-Max, Planar/Iso/Rotor block rotations; no QJL) executed unchanged on CUDA via their torch/Triton path, 3/4-bit labels are their bit-widths (eff. bits = +1 for the fp32-norm layout); `simulated` = our quantise->dequantise reimplementation of the published scheme, not the official code. Simulated: fp8/int8 (plain casts), MXFP4/NVFP4 (OCP/NVIDIA recipes), QServe-style int4 (no SmoothAttention, no weight/act quant), KIVI (K per-channel, V per-token, fp16 residual 128; bytes exclude the residual), KVQuant-style (simplified: post-RoPE, block-fit equal-mass levels, 1% fp16 outliers; real KVQuant uses offline sensitivity-weighted k-means pre-RoPE), UltraQuant paper variants (`uq_fp4_c156`: c=0.156 round scale; `uq_fp4_whtk`: repo scale + WHT on K; `uq_fp4_paper`: c=0.156 + WHT on K + BF16 first/last 2 layers; Q kept bf16 not FP8; bytes ratio excludes the BF16 edge layers).
- **Not run**: SemKV (no public code, scheme underspecified in abstract), STAR-KV (needs per-model training), BitDecoding-FP4 / kvpress quanto (need Blackwell / extra install; out of time), official KIVI/KVQuant/QServe code (CUDA-ext builds, fake-quant reimplementations used instead).
- Planar/Iso/Rotor poor accuracy: checked it is not a Triton-path bug (results/quality_raw/sanity/blockquant_sanity.json: Triton == torch fallback for planar/iso; rotor torch fallback is itself broken, cos 0.41, but we ran Triton, cos 0.98 at 3 bit on Gaussian). On real Mistral layer-10 K the per-vector relative error is ~2x TurboQuant's at 4 bit (planar4 0.21 vs turbo4 0.097; Gaussian: identical 0.097) because 2D/4D block rotations cannot spread outlier channels, and the softmax amplifies this (attention-output cos 0.70-0.77). Agrees with the independent measurement in results/real_kv_summary.md (cos 0.69-0.79). Their MI300X study's quality claims were on a different protocol.
